tailMarker.anomalyNote: No §3.1 anomaly: rank 10, well past the conditioning head. Consequential detail: the marker at 10 places both hydrolyzed proteins (@15, @17) and Panthenol (@11) in the tail. Its near-twin #10 (Bali Curls Deep Repair Mask, near-identical architecture) has its earliest tail-class ingredient at rank 12 (Sodium Benzoate), which places Panthenol above the tail there. See AP-03-TWINS.  ||  PLAUSIBILITY ASSESSMENT (R2, §3.1.1, added under v0.2): PLAUSIBLE. CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2, GLYCINE SOJA OIL @3, BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER @5, CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @6, COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @7 and BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 all outrank PARFUM @10; conventional O/W emulsion with AQUA @1. Neither limb fires. RE-DERIVED UNDER v0.3 (E1, 2026-09-14): R3's tail-edge exclusion is WITHDRAWN. BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9, at tail_index - 1, counts normally toward S1; conditioning_level returns to `high` and the value is capped at `moderate` confidence with a `boundary_position_ingredient` hinweise note - see conditioningLevel. Third plausibility limb (E2, §3.1.1) checked and NOT fired: PARFUM @10 is the fragrance compound itself and no declared allergen outranks it.

conditioningLevel.evidenceScope: Formula-only, above-tail ranks 1–9; category-relative to the German drugstore rinse-out mask shelf.
conditioningLevel.rationale: Re-derived under v0.3 (E1, 2026-09-14). E1 withdraws R3's tail-edge exclusion, so BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 carries S1 in full alongside CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @6. With S1 satisfied and both S2 and S3 firing comfortably, the `high` bar is met with more headroom than any other product in the cohort that moved under E1. Confidence is capped at `moderate` because S1 is load-bearing on a boundary-position species: without BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 the value would be `moderate`. This reverses v0.2's value and closes AP-03-TAILEDGE. It also resolves the twin divergence: this product and its near-twin #10 Bali Curls Deep Repair now agree on field 1, as two near-identical formulas from one brand should. E2 ceiling: comparative structural intensity potential, never measured treatment performance.
evidenceSignals: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE (rank 6) — long-chain cationic quat above the tail (tail_index 10, PARFUM): first distinct S1 species

BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE (rank 9) — a second, structurally distinct long-chain cationic, declared at tail_index − 1. Under E1 (2026-09-14) it COUNTS in full; it is the species S1 hinges on, and the reason confidence is capped at `moderate`
S1 SATISFIED on those two distinct cationic species
CETEARYL ALCOHOL (rank 2) — long-chain fatty alcohol in the top three: S2 SATISFIED, and independent of the boundary band

GLYCINE SOJA OIL (3), BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER (5), COCOS NUCIFERA OIL (7) — three distinct non-fatty-alcohol lipids above the tail, none of them at the boundary: S3 SATISFIED, also independent of the boundary band
PARFUM (rank 10) — tail marker, plausible under §3.1.1 on all three limbs (R2; third limb added E2)
conditioningLevel.derivation: §9.1 on the above-tail segment (ranks 1–9), under E1's boundary-position rule (no species is removed). S1 = SATISFIED: CETRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @6 and BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9. S2 = SATISFIED: CETEARYL ALCOHOL @2. S3 = SATISFIED: three distinct lipids at ranks 3, 5 and 7. All three signals fire; `high` needs S1 plus one of S2/S3 and gets both. Load-bearing boundary check (E1): removing BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 would drop S1 and therefore the value (S2+S3 without S1 is explicitly `moderate`) → the species IS load-bearing → confidence capped at `moderate` and `boundary_position_ingredient` emitted. S2 and S3 are unaffected by the boundary in either direction.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `high`: S1 mandatory plus at least one of S2/S3, with no material counter-signal. S1 fires on two distinct cationics and BOTH S2 and S3 fire independently of the boundary band. D1's multiple-independent-signals breadth is met three times over, across all three signal families.

`moderate` does not apply, and this is the value that MOVED: v0.2 read `moderate` only because R3's tail-edge exclusion struck BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 before the count, leaving S2+S3 without S1 — a combination §9.1 assigns to `moderate` precisely because S2 and S3 both read the fatty/emollient load that §9.2 owns. That reasoning is intact; what changed is that S1 now fires, so the `high` here is not a second reading of the richness already stated in `weight_potential: high`. It is the cationic-breadth reading S1 exists for.
`low` does not apply: all three signals hold.

Material counter-signals checked and NOT fired: resolved, plausible marker on all three §3.1.1 limbs; no §2.4.1 tier-2 conflict; no fired signal resting on a lexicon family-10 species (GLYCERYL STEARATE SE @14 is in the tail and was never counted).

Confidence is `moderate`, not `high`, under §9.1's E1-amended confidence rule: S1 would not fire without a tail_index − 1 species. The sub-drugstore sourcing tier is a second, independent reason the cap would hold anyway.
counterSignals: S1 hinges on one rank: BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE at 9 against PARFUM at 10. Under v0.2's strike this product read `moderate` and its near-twin #10 — same two cationics at @8 and @10 against a marker at 12 — read `high`, so the twins diverged on a two-rank printing difference. Under E1 both read `high` and the divergence is gone; what remains is that #03 carries a confidence cap #10 does not. That is the honest difference between them and the right place for it. See AP-03-TWINS.
Long ingredient list and the rheology-only GLYCERYL STEARATE SE @14 and HYDROXYPROPYL GUAR HYDROXYPROPYLTRIMONIUM CHLORIDE @13 — §9.1 NON-material counter-signals: recorded, never capping.
Two hydrolyzed proteins (@15, @17) sit in the tail behind an 'SOS Protein' pack — a sub-1 % hero tail, recorded in `hinweise` and credited nowhere. It does not touch this field.
Lexicon §13: two distinct above-tail cationics is 'near-baseline in this market', so S1's threshold sits low against the German shelf (§18.1).
limitations: A three-step concentration scale is at the edge of INCI support; no published dataset maps INCI patterns to validated low/medium/high thresholds (§9.1 honest limitation).

Rank is used qualitatively only. EU Art. 19 hides the 1 % boundary; no percentage, ratio, dose or deposited amount is inferable. That is precisely the uncertainty E1's confidence cap encodes on this record.

Reading (a) is unavailable: no R5 species above the tail (both hydrolyzed proteins are tail-side) and the humectant count is two (GLYCERIN @4, BETAINE @8) against a required three. primaryFocus.rationale: Every special-purpose route fails its own test, the D5 moisture guard fails on cluster size, and neither the shine nor the smoothing threshold is reachable without a silicone, polymer, or film former above the tail. What remains is a rich, capable, conventional mask whose distinguishing feature — richness — is the category baseline. §9.5.2 step 8 is the honest answer.

primaryFocus.derivation: Step 1 baseline exclusion applied. Step 2: the four lipids, two cationics and fatty alcohol are ONE M1 observation, not four focus candidates (§6 rule 1). Step 3: `repair` blocked (no R5 above tail, no bond); `curl_support` rejected (see threshold reasoning); `color_care` blocked; `lightness` blocked (weight is `high`). Step 4 `moisture` blocked at cluster size. Step 5 `shine` blocked (§9.5.4 criterion 1 — no alignment-oriented route above the tail, and an R4b heavy lipid IS above the tail). Step 6 `smoothing` rejected. Step 7 `detangling` rejected. Step 8 → `general`.
thresholdReasoning: Clears `general`: §9.5.2 step 8 — a capable conventional mask where no differentiator clears threshold and the formula evidence is nonspecific.

`curl_support` is the closest competitor and is REFUSED on principle. Its test is 'high slip PLUS compatible weight/body architecture', with curl positioning as corroboration only. Both legs are literally satisfiable here — but they are satisfied by nothing except the category baseline (a two-cationic cetearyl base plus lipids), which is exactly what §9.5.2 step 1 forbids from creating a focus. The only thing distinguishing this product from #01 HASK, whose architecture is comparably rich and which gets `general`, is the curl claim — and step 9 states positioning may corroborate but never create. Awarding `curl_support` here would be claim-creation wearing a formula test. See AP-03-CURLBAR.
`moisture` does not apply: the D5 guard needs ≥3 distinct humectants above the tail with ≥2 non-glycerin. Glycerin @4 and Betaine @8 give two, and Panthenol @11 falls one rank below the marker.

`smoothing` does not apply: step 6 requires the architecture to extend materially beyond the ordinary mask base via a distinct silicone, substantive polymer, or substantial lipid/emollient route. The lipid route qualifies for that conjunct, but dry surface control is not this formula's clearest practical differentiator — there is no silicone, no polymer and no film former above the tail, and the credited route is softening rather than surface control.
`detangling` does not apply: slip is category baseline (§9.5.2 step 7's stated expectation), and nothing here makes it distinctive relative to competing routes.

Re-checked under v0.2 (R5). The `moisture` headline was already blocked at §9.5.3 criterion 1 (two above-tail humectants against a required three). Recorded for completeness: criterion 2 limb (i) would also fire, on BUTYROSPERMUM PARKII BUTTER @5 and COCOS NUCIFERA OIL @7 — two R4b heavy lipids above the marker. The headline is doubly blocked and the value is unchanged.
counterSignals: The product's entire identity is protein repair; none of it survives the tail rule, so none of it may create a route.
This product and #10 receive an identical nine-field profile despite occupying different archetype slots (3 'protein bomb' vs 9 'curl mask') — see AP-03-TWINS.
limitations: `general` is a statement about evidence, not about product quality.

blindToFinalChanges.reason: Unblinding changed nothing. adjudicationPoints.title: CLOSED by E1 (2026-09-14) — the tail-edge strike is withdrawn, conditioning_level returns to `high`, and the twin divergence with #10 disappears
adjudicationPoints.body: Raised under v0.2: R3's tail-edge exclusion struck BEHENTRIMONIUM METHOSULFATE @9 (against PARFUM @10), S1 failed, and this product dropped to `moderate` — while its near-twin #10, carrying the same two cationics at @8 and @10 against a marker at @12, kept `high`. Two near-identical formulas from one brand diverged on field 1 because of a two-rank difference in where a preservative was printed. Nick ruled E1 on 2026-09-14: a boundary-position species counts normally and the boundary uncertainty is carried as a confidence cap. conditioning_level therefore returns to `high` at `moderate` confidence, the twins agree again, and the only remaining difference between them is that #03 carries the cap and #10 does not — which is the honest statement of the two-rank difference. The boundary-band WIDTH question that AP-03-TWINS framed is largely defused with it: under E1 no width of band strikes anything, so widening the band could only widen the set of capped values (§9.1, E1). Nothing further is needed from Nick on this record.
